beginner.headline: Tomorrow (Thu Oct 15): conditional for beginners; lower confidence than a same-morning report, and your morning on-site check decides. New 17–18 s south swell building (fewer, stronger sets) and breezier ENE trades, 15–20 kt. Best 6:45–9:30 AM around the 7:13 AM high (1.9 ft), before the wind peaks. Afternoon not recommended for beginners.
beginner.recommendation: Plan for 6:45–9:30 AM: the 7:13 AM high (1.9 ft) gives the most water over the reef, and trades are lightest early (model ENE 16 mph, gusts 22, at 6–7 AM, building to 18 mph, gusts 25, by 9–10 AM; NWS ENE 15–20 kt all day). Expect a different swell from today: the 12–13 s SSW is fading and a 17–18 s south swell is building, so lulls get longer and sets come in fewer but with more push, reaching further inside than the average size suggests. Watch several full set cycles (10+ minutes) before starting. ENE trades are cross-offshore at Waikīkī, so expect seaward drift from the start, worse on gusts. The DOH list was not read, so check water color at Canoes and toward the Kūhiō drains and Ala Wai side; brown, gray or cloudy water ends it. One student or a small group of strong adults; several students or children only if drift is low and sets stay small inside. Your on-site read overrides this report.

water.runoff: Brown, gray, cloudy or turbid water, or visible runoff: don't go in, advisory or not. DOH guidance: storm runoff can carry sewage and pathogens; coastal water usually needs about 48 hours to flush.
